why_go: Peak season to explore West Siang's river valleys. January brings 7-22°C dry weather, ideal for ILP paperwork and rafting season ramp-up on the Siyom. Plan 24-48 hours for permit processing.
February is the driest month for Arunachal trekking. 9-24°C and clear skies unlock Mechuka's high passes and the surrounding Galo tribal villages. Rafting season reaches full strength.
March remains dry at 12-27°C, though pre-monsoon humidity climbs late in the month. This is your last window for the full Mechuka run-on and multi-day rafting before the landscape floods.
April's Mopin festival (Galo new year) peaks mid-month at 15-30°C. Roads remain passable through mid-month. Rafting tails off but pre-monsoon showers inject water into rivers late.

Monsoon arrives early in May (18-30°C, 350-450mm rainfall), opening the landscape but destabilising roads. Landslide windows multiply weekly. Visit only if rain-forest solitude outweighs logistics risk.
why_not: Pre-monsoon rains waterlog trails and trigger frequent landslides on the Aalo-Mechuka corridor, leaving travellers stranded for days.
Full monsoon delivers 600-800mm rainfall, flooding the Siang River and severing road access for weeks. The Aalo-Mechuka route becomes functionally impassable.
Peak monsoon hammers the valley with 700-900mm rainfall. Landslide closures erupt every 5-7 days, stranding vehicles indefinitely. The region is functionally closed.
August monsoon persists with 600-800mm rainfall, leaving roads patchy and trails treacherous. Though Independence Day brings local programmes, travel logistics remain unpredictable.

why_go: Monsoon retreats in September (350-450mm rainfall), and roads stabilise by late month. The landscape is sodden and lush, but rafting remains six weeks away.
why_not: Waterlogged roads from monsoon recovery efforts prevent reliable travel until October.

why_go: October opens the season with 100-150mm rainfall mostly in the first week, 14-26°C temperatures, and fully restored roads. Rafting returns to operational strength.
November peaks at 11-24°C, dry skies, and a reliable road network. Rafting reaches full strength, and pre-Yomgo Festival quiet makes this the window for river and village exploration.
December brings dryest conditions (8-22°C), peak rafting, and fully solid roads. A modest Christmas-New Year bump brings company without overwhelming the river valleys.
January's cool window (10-27°C) offers pleasant daytime exploration of Ujjayanta Palace and nearby forests, though early mornings require layering.
why_not: Cool mornings at 10°C demand light layers despite comfortable daytime warmth.

why_go: February warms to 12-28°C and remains dry, offering peak comfort for trekking through palace grounds and forest reserves.
why_not: Mild February warmth makes trekking genuinely comfortable, though seasonality means fewer organised group activities.

why_go: March's warm 16-32°C window, combined with Holi celebrations and spring foliage, makes this ideal for palace exploration and museum visits without summer heat.
April brings warm 20-34°C weather, the Bengali New Year festivities, and fewer crowds than March.
why_not: Pre-monsoon heat and humidity peak at 75%, making outdoor sightseeing uncomfortable despite cultural celebrations.
May combines extreme pre-monsoon heat (22-35°C) with peak humidity at 80%, and early showers compress outdoor exploration. Outdoor sightseeing becomes unbearable.
Monsoon flooding (24-32°C, heavy rain) renders roads and key attractions inaccessible during peak rains.
Peak monsoon brings very heavy rainfall that closes roads and attractions entirely throughout July.
Monsoon rains continue, leaving roads and attractions inaccessible throughout August.
Tail-end monsoon delivers frequent showers that disrupt outdoor plans and museum visits.

why_go: October's post-monsoon window (18-30°C) coincides with Durga Puja, Tripura's biggest festival. Clear skies, restored roads, and temple rituals make this the year's best month.
November remains pleasant at 14-28°C with minimal rainfall. Post-Puja calm brings smaller crowds for unrushed palace and museum exploration.
December's cool 10-27°C weather and clear skies remain pleasant for sightseeing.
why_not: India's holiday season crowds surge, limiting spontaneity at Ujjayanta Palace and museum sites.

why_go: January peaks at 24-30°C with 30-35m dive visibility and calm seas. Inter-island ferry schedules run fully. Permits require 30-45 days' advance notice; book now.
February, the driest month (24-31°C), brings minimal sea state and school-holiday demand easing mid-month. Dive visibility remains excellent. Permit lead still 30-45 days.
March stays clean at 26-32°C before pre-monsoon humidity climbs late month. Dive operators run at full capacity. Permit timelines remain 30-45 days.
April brings 28-33°C heat and 80% humidity, but seas remain calm. Resorts slip into off-peak pricing despite functional dive operations.
May's late pre-monsoon conditions (28-33°C) still allow early-month diving, though the southwest monsoon advance closes most islands by June 1.
why_not: Pre-monsoon swells trigger unpredictable water conditions and ferry schedule cancellations.
Southwest monsoon (25-29°C, 300-400mm rain) churns seas to unsafe levels. Alliance Air suspends flights and most resorts close entirely.
Peak monsoon closes the chain and halts permit issuance for July dates entirely.
August monsoon rains continue with 300-400mm rainfall. Though Independence Day brings security protocols, functional access remains impossible.

why_go: September's retreating monsoon (200-250mm rain, mostly first half) allows late-month arrivals only. Permits open incrementally as weather stabilises.
why_not: Unreliable flights to Agatti, frequently cancelled due to monsoon weather, make September risky.

why_go: October's season opening (100-150mm rain, mostly first week) brings restored Alliance Air schedules and dive visibility returning to 25m+. 24-31°C conditions are pleasant.
November builds momentum at 23-30°C with 50-80mm rain. NE monsoon largely spares Lakshadweep. Permit lead reverts to 30-45 days.
December peaks at 22-29°C with dry conditions and 30-35m dive visibility. Christmas-New Year premium pricing is steep. Alliance Air books out 60 days ahead.
January peaks at 18-31°C with dry seas and olive ridley turtle nesting. Post-New Year rates ease 15%, and yoga retreats run at full capacity.
February, the driest month (19-31°C), sustains peak turtle nesting. Hotel rates ease another 15% after January surge. The beach remains empty and calm.
March's cool window (21-33°C) brings the last month before summer heat. Turtle nesting tails off. Yoga retreats wrap by mid-month. Rates sit 25% below January peaks.
April's pre-monsoon heat (24-35°C) reduces tourism pressure and drops rates further.
why_not: April heat peaks while the beach scene shuts down for summer, leaving accommodations half-closed and activity limited.

why_go: May's late pre-monsoon conditions (26-37°C) bring empty beaches and rock-bottom rates, though shacks dismantle by May 31.
why_not: Monsoon shutters beach shacks and tourist infrastructure through June, rendering visitor amenities unavailable.
Southwest monsoon arrives June 10 with 600-800mm rainfall, red-flag seas, and all beach shacks closed. The shore becomes unsafe.
Peak monsoon (24-29°C, 900-1100mm rainfall) closes the beach entirely. Shacks remain shuttered and the sea stays dangerous.
August monsoon persists with 700-900mm rainfall and all beach infrastructure closed. The shore is off-limits.

why_go: September's retreating monsoon (25-30°C, 300-400mm rain) begins reopening shacks by late month. Turtle nesting restarts in late September.
why_not: Heavy monsoon rains persist through early September, keeping beaches closed and unreliable for travel.

why_go: October's reopening (23-32°C, 150-200mm rain) marks shack restoration on October 1. Olive ridley nesting begins. The season resumes.
November peaks at 20-30°C with rainfall under 30mm. Olive ridley nesting reaches peak activity. Yoga retreats fill quickly.
December's peak season (18-29°C, dry) brings 50-70% rate premiums over November. Christmas-New Year bookings require 3+ weeks' advance notice.
January's architecture laboratory window (15-29°C, dry) showcases the Lad Khan and Durga temples at the year's cleanest light. Stone detail photography peaks.
February, the driest month (17-32°C), delivers year-best conditions for photographing the 120+ temples. Stone-detail clarity is unmatched. Day-trips from Badami hit peak comfort.
March's cool window (19-35°C) offers the last comfortable month for open-air temple exploration. Rates ease 25% as summer approaches.

why_not: April heat dome opens with 23-41°C temperatures, making mid-day temple walking unworkable. The 120-temple cluster becomes physically unbearable.
May's extreme heat (25-43°C) and pre-monsoon dust make outdoor temple exploration impossible. The landscape is hazy and brutal.

why_go: June's light monsoon (24-36°C, 50-70mm rain) eases heat but compresses walking windows to mornings and evenings. October is the cleaner restart.
why_not: Monsoon rains obscure stone details and muddy paths, frustrating temple exploration despite reduced heat.

why_go: July monsoon (23-32°C, 80-110mm rain) brings a green landscape. Stone walks remain viable in morning and evening pockets.
why_not: Relentless monsoon rains make temple exploration muddy and frustrating, undermining the architectural focus.

why_go: August monsoon (22-30°C, 70-100mm rain) sustains green fields. Morning and evening walks work around afternoon showers.
why_not: Monsoon flooding blocks temple access and makes site exploration unsafe for extended stays.

why_go: September's retreating monsoon (21-29°C, 50-70mm rain) peaks the green landscape. This is the last off-peak window before October crowds.
why_not: Monsoon rains interrupt temple exploration more than enhance it, despite the vibrant landscape.

why_go: October's opening (19-30°C, 30-50mm rain) restores green fields without heavy downpours. Cluster walks resume mid-month as conditions stabilise.
November peaks at 17-28°C with dry conditions. Karnataka Rajyotsava (Nov 1) adds cultural context. Stone-detail photography reaches year-best air clarity.
December's peak season (14-27°C, dry) sees moderate Christmas-NYE spikes. Stone detail photography hits year-cleanest air and light.
January's cool window (8-20°C) offers clear ridge views and pleasant conditions, though most shops close on Sundays.
why_not: Sunday business shutdowns limit activities despite clear skies and good visibility.

why_go: February warms to 9-21°C and remains dry, with fewer crowds than peak season though visibility remains clear.
why_not: Dry February means fewer crowds and clearer hill views, marking the tail of peak season comfort.

why_go: March's warm window (12-24°C) aligns with Chapchar Kut, Mizoram's biggest tribal festival. Spring foliage peaks. Churches and cultural sites shine.
April's pleasant warm conditions (14-26°C) arrive as humidity rises sharply mid-month.
why_not: Pre-monsoon humidity rises sharply after mid-April, making late April uncomfortable for trekking.
Pre-monsoon rains intensify through May, limiting outdoor activities and reducing trekking visibility.
Monsoon landslides close hill roads unpredictably for weeks, stranding visitors and disrupting transport.
Peak monsoon rains wash out roads and leave travellers stranded for days during heavy downpours.
August monsoon keeps roads slippery at this elevation, with frequent landslides and washouts.
Post-monsoon roads remain waterlogged. Trekking and sightseeing are hampered by mud and slippery terrain.

why_go: October's post-monsoon window (12-24°C) clears to blue skies and green hillsides. Visibility peaks and cultural activities resume.
November cools to 10-22°C with clear, dry conditions. Cultural events return. Visibility peaks for ridge-walk photography.
December's cool window (8-20°C) peaks with Christmas, Mizoram's biggest celebration. Churches light up, community feasting fills the city with warmth.
January's peak backwater season (23-31°C, dry) brings calm Punnamada Lake and post-New Year rate eases. Houseboat schedules run at full capacity.
February, the driest month (24-32°C), tightens houseboat availability late month as shoulder operators book. Water clarity is year-best.
March's cool window (25-33°C) brings 20% rate drops as summer nears. Water temperature climbs, compressing the ideal houseboat window.
April's pre-monsoon heat (27-34°C, 80% humidity) reduces tourism but slashes rates significantly. AC houseboats manage the heat.
why_not: Peak heat and humidity drain the backwater's charm; non-AC cabins become uncomfortably warm.

why_go: May combines peak heat (28-34°C, 85% humidity) with pre-monsoon conditions. Late-month cruise schedules thin. Rock-bottom rates reward heat tolerance.
why_not: Pre-monsoon heat and 85% humidity make houseboat cabins uncomfortably warm unless booking AC options.

why_go: June's monsoon onset (25-30°C, 600-700mm rain) brings the Champakulam Boat Race during June Moolam. The landscape greens dramatically.
why_not: Monsoon downpours make houseboat travel uncomfortable and backwater visibility poor.

why_go: July's peak monsoon (25-29°C, 700-800mm rain) aligns with Karkidakam Ayurveda season mid-month. Houseboats offer therapeutic immersion.
why_not: Monsoon rains make backwater navigation treacherous and houseboat trips frequently cancelled.

why_go: August combines monsoon (25-29°C, 500-600mm rain), Onam, and the Nehru Trophy (2nd Saturday). Rope boat races electrify the canals despite showers.
why_not: Monsoon floods backwaters and obscure the landscape that draws visitors here.

why_go: September's monsoon retreat (25-30°C, 350-400mm rain) brings Onam tail and the Aranmula Boat Race. The Aranmula ceremony remains photogenic.
why_not: Monsoon rains taper but afternoons stay wet; houseboat canals fill while humidity peaks.

why_go: October's season opening (24-31°C, 200-250mm late spillover) restores houseboat schedules and water clarity. Birdlife peaks.
November peaks at 23-30°C with rainfall under 50mm. Houseboat schedules reach full capacity. Migratory birds turn the sanctuary into a haven.
December's peak season (22-30°C, dry) brings 2.5-3x Christmas-NYE rate premiums. Houseboat lead time stretches to 4-6 weeks.
January (14-26°C at Topslip 800m) opens the year-round reserve with good wildlife concentration. Jeep safari costs ₹2500-4500. Note: Reserve closes Monday mornings.
why_not: Early-morning safari visibility suffers from persistent fog during peak wildlife activity hours.

why_go: February peaks at 15-28°C with the year's best wildlife concentration. Tiger sighting odds climb dramatically. Karian Shola trek peaks. Closed Mondays.
March sustains peak wildlife at 16-30°C. Tiger and elephant sightings hit year-best odds. Karian Shola trek remains optimal. Monday closures apply.
April's warm window (18-32°C) continues peak wildlife. Tiger sighting odds remain at year-best. Pre-monsoon storms confine to the last 10 days.
May's pre-monsoon peak (19-32°C) remains workable for the first fortnight. Wildlife concentrates before dispersing. Last 10 days bring SW monsoon advances.
June's SW monsoon onset (17-25°C, 300-500mm rain) brings lush green landscapes. Some zones close as wildlife disperses into forest cover.

why_not: Peak monsoon (17-24°C, 500-800mm rain) closes most zones. The Topslip-Pollachi road becomes erratic, and wildlife spotting becomes nearly impossible.
August monsoon (17-24°C, 400-600mm rain) keeps most zones closed. Wildlife spotting remains nearly impossible amid deluge.

why_go: September's retreating monsoon (17-25°C, 250-400mm rain) brings reduced operations. October offers a cleaner restart.
why_not: Monsoon rains make trails muddy and wildlife spotting nearly impossible in September.

why_go: October's season opening (16-25°C, 150-250mm rain) restores full safari operations. Wildlife patterns return to normal. Booking is essential.
why_not: Monsoon runoff leaves forest roads unpredictably impassable mid-month despite conditions stabilising.

why_go: November builds to high season at 14-24°C. Wildlife visibility improves steadily. Rates climb 15% through the month. Reserve closed Mondays.
why_not: NE-monsoon rains keep trails boggy and reduce visibility for tiger spotting.

why_go: December peaks at 13-24°C. Forest rest houses book 6-8 weeks ahead. Christmas-New Year rates climb 20%. Reserve closed Mondays.
why_not: Early December fog blankets trails, limiting tiger sightings when visibility matters most.

why_go: January's peak Konkan winter (21-31°C, dry) brings post-New Year rate eases. The Wednesday Flea Market swings into full operation.
February, the driest month (22-32°C), peaks the Flea Market and Carnival float parade window. The beach scene hits its stride.
March's cool window (23-33°C) brings Shigmo parade mid-month. Hotel rates slide 20-25%. Beach vibes remain strong through month-end.
April's pre-monsoon heat (25-35°C, 75% humidity) slows the scene, but beachside shacks operate through May 31 at discounted rates.
why_not: Peak heat arrives as the beach scene shuts down for summer, leaving tourist infrastructure reduced.

why_go: May's peak pre-monsoon heat (26-36°C, 80% humidity) compounds with shack dismantling by month-end. Solitude seekers thrive.
why_not: Monsoon shutters beach shacks and tourist infrastructure through June, rendering visitor amenities unavailable.
Southwest monsoon arrives June 10 with 700-800mm rainfall, red-flag seas, and all beach shacks closed. The shore is unsafe.
Peak monsoon (24-29°C, 900-1100mm rain) closes the beach entirely. All shacks shut. The sea stays dangerous.
August monsoon persists with 500-700mm rain. Beach remains unsafe, all shacks closed. Skip Anjuna proper.

why_go: September's monsoon retreat (24-31°C, 250-300mm rain) begins rebuilding shacks for October 1 reopening. The beach gradually awakens.
why_not: Heavy monsoon rains persist actively. Beaches remain closed and infrastructure is still being repaired.

why_go: October's season opening (Oct 1, 24-32°C, 100-150mm spillover) rebuilds shacks and restores the Wednesday Flea. The scene returns.
November peaks at 22-31°C with rainfall under 30mm. International DJs return. The Wednesday Flea hits full capacity and vibrancy.
December's peak season (21-30°C, dry) sees Christmas-NYE rates triple Dec 22-Jan 5. The sunburn diaspora fills Curlies and beach shacks.
